deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE (inferred). The page continues the previous folio. There, five angles α…ε with rational tangents were sought, given as fractions with angles in degrees, minutes and seconds. Here Gauss works out a general parametrisation of such a quintuple and a two-parameter family of solutions. Primes mark a related set of quantities; their exact meaning cannot be settled from this page.

SETUP. A, B are coprime with A > B. a, b are coprime with a > b. Gauss writes 'Pr.Z. u. s.', i.e. 'Primzahlen unter sich', meaning coprime. Set p = Aa, q = Ba, r = Ab, s = Bb.

DEFINITIONS (first column).
- α' = b/a
- β = B/A
- γ' = √[(q+r)(q−r) / ((p−s)(p+s))]
- δ = √[(q−r)(p+s) / ((q+r)(p−s))]
- ε' = √[(q−r)(p−s) / ((q+r)(p+s))]

All three radicands differ from (q²−r²)(p²−s²) only by a square factor. So the single condition (B²a² − A²b²)(A²a² − B²b²) = □ makes γ', δ, ε' rational at once. That is the quartic-type Diophantine condition being studied.

RELATIONS IN α', β (lower half). Divide by A²a²:
- γ'² = (β² − α'²) / (1 − α'²β²), equivalently α'²β²γ'² = α'² − β² + γ'².
- δ² = [(β−α')/(β+α')] · [(1+βα')/(1−βα')]. A first attempt, written in α, β and with the factors arranged differently, is struck out.
- ε'² = [(β−α')/(β+α')] · [(1−βα')/(1+βα')].
- Hence δε' = (β−α')/(β+α') and ε'/δ = (1−βα')/(1+βα').
- From these, γ' = (δ−ε') / (β(1−δε')) = (δ−ε')(β+α') / (2α'β) = (δ−ε')(β−α') / (2α'βδε').

The last two forms follow from 1 − δε' = 2α'/(β+α'). The first needs δ²(β+α')² = γ'²(1+βα')², which holds identically (my verification).

In angle language (my gloss): with α' = tan x, β = tan y, u = y−x, v = y+x, one has γ'² = tan u·tan v, ε'² = tan u / tan v and δ² = sin 2u / sin 2v.

Two further expressions, (α−β')/(1−αβ') and (α+β')/(1+αβ'), are written beside δε' and ε'/δ in unprimed/primed variables. Their product has exactly the γ'² form. Their precise intended meaning cannot be determined from this page.

DERIVED QUANTITIES (middle column):
- T1 = ab(A²−B²) / (AB(a²+b²))
- T2 = ab(A²+B²) / (AB(a²−b²))
- T3 = 2abAB / √[(p²−s²)(q²−r²)]
- T4 = [(q²+r²)/(p²+s²)] · √[(p²−s²)/(q²−r²)]
- T5 = √[(q²−r²)/(p²−s²)] = γ'

With α' = tan x and β = tan y, T2 = tan 2x / sin 2y and T1 = sin 2x · cot 2y. These are tan A and cot B in a right spherical triangle with legs 2x, 2y (my identification, tentative).

The column headed 'auch' ('also') adds three more expressions:
- (A²−B²)√[(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] / (AB(a²−b²)(A²+B²))
- (A²+B²)√[(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] / (AB(a²+b²)(A²−B²))
- 2AB√[(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] / (ab(A⁴−B⁴))
Then comes an expression marked 'Gut': [(b²(A⁴+B⁴) + 2a²A²B²) / (a²(A⁴+B⁴) − 2b²A²B²)] · a/b, followed by b/a. A struck fraction with denominator A²(p²−s²) + B²(q²−r²) appears at far right. These are not checked numerically on the page, and I could not identify which quantity they represent.

NUMERICAL EXAMPLES.

(1) A = 37, B = 29, a = 7, b = 4, so p = 259, q = 203, r = 148, s = 116.
- α' = 4/7, β = 29/37, γ' = 3/5, δ = 25/39, ε' = 11/45.
- T1 = 14784/69745, T2 = 61880/35409, T3 = 60088/32175, T4 = 315565/241611, T5 = 3/5.
- Here (p²−s²)(q²−r²) = 53625 · 19305 = 32175².

(2) A = 5, B = 4, a = 13, b = 4, so p = 65, q = 52, r = 20, s = 16.
- α' = 4/13, β = 4/5, γ' = 16/21, δ = 6/7, ε' = 14/27.
- T1 = 117/925, T2 = 533/765, T3 = 130/189, T4 = 4074/4481, T5 = 16/21.
- Here 3969 · 2304 = (63·48)².

I recomputed every entry and all are correct.

INFINITE FAMILIES (bottom). 'The condition of p. 1' can be reconstructed as (a²−b²)(a'²−b'²)·a·b·a'·b' = □, where a, b, a', b' are new letters. This matches the next page's formulation with (p, q, P, Q). The identification is mine, but it makes all three of Gauss's cases work.
- Case I: a = g, b = h, a' = g ± h, b' = 2h. The product equals (g−h)²(g+h)²h² · 2g(g ± 3h). So the condition reduces to (2g ± 6h) : g being a ratio of two squares.
- Case II: a = h, b = g, a' = 2h, b' = h−g. The product equals (h−g)²(h+g)²h² · 2g(3h−g). So the condition reduces to (6h−2g) : g = □ : □.
- Third variant: a = h+g, b = g, a' = h+2g, b' = g. The product equals (h+g)²(h+2g)²g² · h(h+3g). So the condition reduces to (h+3g) : h = □ : □. Gauss notes this 'ist nicht wesentlich verschieden' (is not essentially different).

Each case is a conic with obvious rational points, hence 'auf unendlich viele Arten' (in infinitely many ways). This is the standard trick of making the quartic collapse to a quadratic by a linear ansatz.
errors: No mathematical errors found in the surviving (non-struck) formulas or in the numerical tables; all ten numerical values per example check exactly.
The struck-out first version of δδ, written as (α−β)(1−αβ)/((α+β)(1+αβ)) in unprimed variables, was abandoned and correctly replaced by (β−α')/(β+α')·(1+βα')/(1−βα').

Numerical corrections visible on the page: in the T3 entry the numerator was first written 6008 and corrected to 60088; in the T4 entry the denominator 241611 has a corrected first digit. The final values are right.

The side expressions (α−β')/(1−αβ') and (α+β')/(1+αβ') do not follow from the displayed formulas under any obvious reading of the primes (reciprocal, complement); their meaning is unclear rather than demonstrably wrong.
The 'Gut' expression and the 'auch' expressions are not verified on the page, and I could not match them to T1–T5; I cannot confirm what they equal.

results.what: Parametrisation of rational α', β, γ', δ, ε' with γ'² = (β²−α'²)/(1−α'²β²), δε' = (β−α')/(β+α'), ε'/δ = (1−βα')/(1+βα'); all three are rational iff (B²a²−A²b²)(A²a²−B²b²) is a square
results.modern_name: Rational points on a quartic of the form y² = (β²−x²)(1−β²x²) (a genus-1 / Jacobi-quartic-type curve), i.e. rational-tangent angle configurations
results.usually_credited_to: Diophantine tradition (Diophantus, Fermat, Euler); a classical type of problem

results.what: Two worked numerical solutions, (A,B,a,b) = (37,29,7,4) and (5,4,13,4), with derived rational tangents T1–T5
Infinite families satisfying (a²−b²)(a'²−b'²)aba'b' = □ via linear ansatz (a=g, b=h, a'=g±h, b'=2h, etc.), reducing the condition to a conic such as 2g(g±3h) = □
results.modern_name: Reduction of a quartic Diophantine condition to a conic by a special linear substitution (Euler-style ansatz)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard Diophantine and trigonometric work: an elimination giving a single square condition, two explicit rational solutions and conic-reducible special families. The companion page's duplication-type map and cos/sin parametrisation hints at the genus-1 structure, but nothing on this page goes beyond 18th-century Euler-style technique.
